Chapter 25 — Trigonometric Functions and Equations

Kanna, an angle tells us how far a ray has turned. Sine and cosine tell us the vertical and horizontal coordinates of a point on a circle. Start with this picture; the identities will then connect to something you can see.

Your target remains 200 marks: Physics 60, Maths 60, Chemistry 80. Here, accurate signs, domains and angle counting matter as much as remembering formulas.

Concept C01 — Degrees, radians and a full turn

A full turn is 360∘360^\circ360∘. It is also 2π2\pi2π radians. A radian measures an angle using arc length:

θ=arc lengthradius,180∘=π radians.\boxed{\theta=\frac{\text{arc length}}{\text{radius}}}, \qquad \boxed{180^\circ=\pi\text{ radians}}.θ=radiusarc length​​,180∘=π radians​.

For a circle of radius rrr, an angle θ\thetaθ in radians gives arc length rθr\thetarθ and sector area 12r2θ\frac12r^2\theta21​r2θ.

θrad=θdegreeπ180,θdegree=θrad180π.\boxed{\theta_{\rm rad}=\theta_{\rm degree}\frac{\pi}{180}}, \qquad \boxed{\theta_{\rm degree}=\theta_{\rm rad}\frac{180}{\pi}}.θrad​=θdegree​180π​​,θdegree​=θrad​π180​​.

Thus 30∘=π/630^\circ=\pi/630∘=π/6, 45∘=π/445^\circ=\pi/445∘=π/4, 60∘=π/360^\circ=\pi/360∘=π/3, 90∘=π/290^\circ=\pi/290∘=π/2. One radian is about 57.3∘57.3^\circ57.3∘, much larger than 1∘1^\circ1∘.

Read the notation: sin⁡30∘\sin30^\circsin30∘ uses degrees; sin⁡30\sin30sin30 ordinarily means 30 radians. In calculus formulas and the graphs here, angles use radians unless a degree mark is shown.

Concept C02 — What sine, cosine and tangent actually measure

Draw a circle of radius 1. Start at (1,0)(1,0)(1,0) and turn anticlockwise through θ\thetaθ. The new point is

P=(cos⁡θ,sin⁡θ).\boxed{P=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)}.P=(cosθ,sinθ)​.

Cosine is its signed horizontal coordinate; sine is its signed vertical coordinate. Signed means left/below can be negative. They are numbers, not new arrows.

Read the picture: the horizontal projection falls left of the origin, so cosine is negative. The vertical coordinate is above the origin, so sine is positive. The radius stays 1.

For an acute angle in a right triangle, divide both legs by its hypotenuse:

sin⁡θ=opposite leghypotenuse,cos⁡θ=adjacent leghypotenuse,tan⁡θ=opposite legadjacent leg.\sin\theta=\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}, \quad \cos\theta=\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}, \quad \tan\theta=\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}.sinθ=hypotenuseopposite leg​,cosθ=hypotenuseadjacent leg​,tanθ=adjacent legopposite leg​.

The adjacent leg touches the angle; the opposite leg faces it. The hypotenuse faces the right angle and is the longest side.

On the circle,

tan⁡θ=sin⁡θcos⁡θ,cot⁡θ=cos⁡θsin⁡θ,sec⁡θ=1cos⁡θ,csc⁡θ=1sin⁡θ.\boxed{\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}}, \quad \cot\theta=\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}, \quad \sec\theta=\frac1{\cos\theta}, \quad \csc\theta=\frac1{\sin\theta}.tanθ=cosθsinθ​​,cotθ=sinθcosθ​,secθ=cosθ1​,cscθ=sinθ1​.

A zero denominator makes the expression undefined. Do not write tan⁡(π/2)=∞\tan(\pi/2)=\inftytan(π/2)=∞ as an ordinary real value.

Concept C03 — Waves, domains, ranges and periods

As the point moves, its height makes the sine wave and its horizontal coordinate makes the cosine wave.

Read the axes: the horizontal coordinate is the angle, not the circle's horizontal coordinate. The vertical coordinate is a function value. At angle zero, sine starts at 0 and cosine at 1.

sin⁡x\sin xsinx none [−1,1][-1,1][−1,1] 2π2\pi2π
cos⁡x\cos xcosx none [−1,1][-1,1][−1,1] 2π2\pi2π
tan⁡x\tan xtanx π/2+nπ\pi/2+n\piπ/2+nπ R\mathbb RR π\piπ
cot⁡x\cot xcotx nπn\pinπ R\mathbb RR π\piπ
sec⁡x\sec xsecx π/2+nπ\pi/2+n\piπ/2+nπ (−∞,−1]∪[1,∞)(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)(−∞,−1]∪[1,∞) 2π2\pi2π
csc⁡x\csc xcscx nπn\pinπ (−∞,−1]∪[1,∞)(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)(−∞,−1]∪[1,∞) 2π2\pi2π

Here n∈Zn\in\mathbb Zn∈Z means any integer, positive,zero or negative.

Never connect a graph through an undefined input. On each interval between its gaps, tangent increases.

Useful monotonic intervals:

sin⁡x increases on [−π/2,π/2],cos⁡x decreases on [0,π].\sin x\text{ increases on }[-\pi/2,\pi/2],\qquad \cos x\text{ decreases on }[0,\pi].sinx increases on [−π/2,π/2],cosx decreases on [0,π].

Sine does not increase on all of [0,π][0,\pi][0,π]: after π/2\pi/2π/2 it comes down. Use reflection sin⁡(π−x)=sin⁡x\sin(\pi-x)=\sin xsin(π−x)=sinx when comparing two angles on opposite sides of the peak.

Concept C04 — Signs, symmetry and related angles

Divide a full turn into four quadrants:

Quadrant Angle in one turn Sine Cosine Tangent
I (0,π/2)(0,\pi/2)(0,π/2) +++ +++ +++
II (π/2,π)(\pi/2,\pi)(π/2,π) +++ −-− −-−
III (π,3π/2)(\pi,3\pi/2)(π,3π/2) −-− −-− +++
IV (3π/2,2π)(3\pi/2,2\pi)(3π/2,2π) −-− +++ −-−

Axis angles are checked separately. A coordinate can be zero there.

Reflection in the horizontal axis changes only height:

sin⁡(−x)=−sin⁡x,cos⁡(−x)=cos⁡x,tan⁡(−x)=−tan⁡x.\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\quad \cos(-x)=\cos x,\quad \tan(-x)=-\tan x.sin(−x)=−sinx,cos(−x)=cosx,tan(−x)=−tanx.

Half-turn and complementary-angle connections:

sin⁡(π−x)=sin⁡x,cos⁡(π−x)=−cos⁡x,sin⁡(π+x)=−sin⁡x,cos⁡(π+x)=−cos⁡x,sin⁡(π/2−x)=cos⁡x,cos⁡(π/2−x)=sin⁡x.\begin{aligned} \sin(\pi-x)&=\sin x,&\cos(\pi-x)&=-\cos x,\\ \sin(\pi+x)&=-\sin x,&\cos(\pi+x)&=-\cos x,\\ \sin(\pi/2-x)&=\cos x,&\cos(\pi/2-x)&=\sin x. \end{aligned}sin(π−x)sin(π+x)sin(π/2−x)​=sinx,=−sinx,=cosx,​cos(π−x)cos(π+x)cos(π/2−x)​=−cosx,=−cosx,=sinx.​

Adding 2nπ2n\pi2nπ leaves sine and cosine unchanged; adding nπn\pinπ leaves tangent unchanged where defined. Use circle signs to reconstruct identities rather than guessing a sign.

Concept C05 — Angle addition and subtraction

Rotating through AAA and then BBB is one rotation through A+BA+BA+B. Its coordinates give

sin⁡(A±B)=sin⁡Acos⁡B±cos⁡Asin⁡B,\boxed{\sin(A\pm B)=\sin A\cos B\pm\cos A\sin B},sin(A±B)=sinAcosB±cosAsinB​, cos⁡(A±B)=cos⁡Acos⁡B∓sin⁡Asin⁡B.\boxed{\cos(A\pm B)=\cos A\cos B\mp\sin A\sin B}.cos(A±B)=cosAcosB∓sinAsinB​.

The minus sign in cos⁡(A+B)\cos(A+B)cos(A+B) matters. For A=B=π/2A=B=\pi/2A=B=π/2, it must give cos⁡π=−1\cos\pi=-1cosπ=−1.

Dividing sine by cosine gives

tan⁡(A±B)=tan⁡A±tan⁡B1∓tan⁡Atan⁡B,\boxed{\tan(A\pm B)=\frac{\tan A\pm\tan B}{1\mp\tan A\tan B}},tan(A±B)=1∓tanAtanBtanA±tanB​​,

when the displayed tangents and denominator are defined. If the denominator is zero, examine the angle with sine/cosine rather than forcing a finite fraction.

Recognition: an expression such as cos⁡Acos⁡B−sin⁡Asin⁡B\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin BcosAcosB−sinAsinB is already one cosine of a sum. Do not expand it into more pieces.

Useful special-angle route: 15∘=45∘−30∘15^\circ=45^\circ-30^\circ15∘=45∘−30∘ gives

sin⁡15∘=6−24,cos⁡15∘=6+24,tan⁡15∘=2−3.\sin15^\circ=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}, \quad \cos15^\circ=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}, \quad \tan15^\circ=2-\sqrt3.sin15∘=46​−2​​,cos15∘=46​+2​​,tan15∘=2−3​.

Concept C06 — The circle identity and polynomial substitutions

The point lies on the unit circle, so Pythagoras gives

sin⁡2x+cos⁡2x=1.\boxed{\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1}.sin2x+cos2x=1​.

Here sin⁡2x\sin^2xsin2x means (sin⁡x)2(\sin x)^2(sinx)2, not sin⁡(x2)\sin(x^2)sin(x2).

Dividing by the appropriate nonzero square gives

1+tan⁡2x=sec⁡2x,1+cot⁡2x=csc⁡2x.\boxed{1+\tan^2x=\sec^2x}, \qquad \boxed{1+\cot^2x=\csc^2x}.1+tan2x=sec2x​,1+cot2x=csc2x​.

When only even powers appear, try

t=sin⁡2x∈[0,1],cos⁡2x=1−t.t=\sin^2x\in[0,1],\qquad \cos^2x=1-t.t=sin2x∈[0,1],cos2x=1−t.

For example,

sin⁡2x+cos⁡4x=t+(1−t)2=(t−12)2+34.\sin^2x+\cos^4x=t+(1-t)^2 =\left(t-\frac12\right)^2+\frac34.sin2x+cos4x=t+(1−t)2=(t−21​)2+43​.

The square gives a lower bound; the interval 0≤t≤10\le t\le10≤t≤1 also gives an upper bound. Never optimize the polynomial over all real ttt when it represents a restricted trigonometric value.

For s=sin⁡xs=\sin xs=sinx, use s∈[−1,1]s\in[-1,1]s∈[−1,1]. This range decides whether an algebraic root corresponds to a real angle.

Concept C07 — One shifted wave: amplitude and range

For real a,ba,ba,b, let R=a2+b2>0R=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}>0R=a2+b2​>0. Choose ϕ\phiϕ so that cos⁡ϕ=a/R\cos\phi=a/Rcosϕ=a/R, sin⁡ϕ=b/R\sin\phi=b/Rsinϕ=b/R. Then

asin⁡x+bcos⁡x=Rsin⁡(x+ϕ).\boxed{a\sin x+b\cos x=R\sin(x+\phi)}.asinx+bcosx=Rsin(x+ϕ)​.

The amplitude RRR is the distance from the middle height to a peak:

−R≤asin⁡x+bcos⁡x≤R.\boxed{-R\le a\sin x+b\cos x\le R}.−R≤asinx+bcosx≤R​.

Both bounds are attained when xxx can vary over a full turn. Adding a constant ccc shifts the middle:

range of asin⁡x+bcos⁡x+c=[c−R,c+R].\boxed{\text{range of }a\sin x+b\cos x+c=[c-R,c+R]}.range of asinx+bcosx+c=[c−R,c+R]​.

If a=b=0a=b=0a=b=0, the function is constant ccc. A restricted angle interval may prevent a peak from being reached; check its domain.

For 3cos⁡x+sin⁡x\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x3​cosx+sinx, use 2cos⁡(x−π/6)2\cos(x-\pi/6)2cos(x−π/6). Expand your chosen shifted wave once to check the sign.

Why adding separate maxima can fail: sine and cosine cannot both be 1 at the same angle. Their coordinates obey a shared circle constraint.

Concept C08 — Double, triple and half angles

Set A=B=xA=B=xA=B=x in addition formulas:

sin⁡2x=2sin⁡xcos⁡x,\boxed{\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x},sin2x=2sinxcosx​, cos⁡2x=cos⁡2x−sin⁡2x=1−2sin⁡2x=2cos⁡2x−1,\boxed{\cos2x=\cos^2x-\sin^2x =1-2\sin^2x=2\cos^2x-1},cos2x=cos2x−sin2x=1−2sin2x=2cos2x−1​, tan⁡2x=2tan⁡x1−tan⁡2x.\boxed{\tan2x=\frac{2\tan x}{1-\tan^2x}}.tan2x=1−tan2x2tanx​​.

Choose the cosine form that leaves the fewest different functions.

Power reduction:

sin⁡2x=1−cos⁡2x2,cos⁡2x=1+cos⁡2x2.\boxed{\sin^2x=\frac{1-\cos2x}{2}}, \qquad \boxed{\cos^2x=\frac{1+\cos2x}{2}}.sin2x=21−cos2x​​,cos2x=21+cos2x​​.

Triple angles:

sin⁡3x=3sin⁡x−4sin⁡3x,cos⁡3x=4cos⁡3x−3cos⁡x,\sin3x=3\sin x-4\sin^3x,\quad \cos3x=4\cos^3x-3\cos x,sin3x=3sinx−4sin3x,cos3x=4cos3x−3cosx, tan⁡3x=3t−t31−3t2,t=tan⁡x,\tan3x=\frac{3t-t^3}{1-3t^2},\qquad t=\tan x,tan3x=1−3t23t−t3​,t=tanx,

with tangent-domain checks. Square-root half-angle forms need the actual quadrant sign:

sin⁡x2=±1−cos⁡x2,cos⁡x2=±1+cos⁡x2.\sin\frac x2=\pm\sqrt{\frac{1-\cos x}{2}}, \quad \cos\frac x2=\pm\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos x}{2}}.sin2x​=±21−cosx​​,cos2x​=±21+cosx​​.

Where the fractions exist,

tan⁡x2=sin⁡x1+cos⁡x=1−cos⁡xsin⁡x.\boxed{\tan\frac x2=\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x} =\frac{1-\cos x}{\sin x}}.tan2x​=1+cosxsinx​=sinx1−cosx​​.

If t=tan⁡(x/2)t=\tan(x/2)t=tan(x/2) is finite,

sin⁡x=2t1+t2,cos⁡x=1−t21+t2,tan⁡x=2t1−t2.\boxed{\sin x=\frac{2t}{1+t^2}},\quad \boxed{\cos x=\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}},\quad \tan x=\frac{2t}{1-t^2}.sinx=1+t22t​​,cosx=1+t21−t2​​,tanx=1−t22t​.

This substitution omits x=(2n+1)πx=(2n+1)\pix=(2n+1)π, where ttt is undefined. Check those angles separately in the original equation. The last tangent formula also needs t≠±1t\ne\pm1t=±1.

Concept C09 — Turn sums into products,and products into sums

These identities come from adding or subtracting the angle-addition formulas:

sin⁡A+sin⁡B=2sin⁡A+B2cos⁡A−B2,\boxed{\sin A+\sin B =2\sin\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}},sinA+sinB=2sin2A+B​cos2A−B​​, sin⁡A−sin⁡B=2cos⁡A+B2sin⁡A−B2,\sin A-\sin B=2\cos\frac{A+B}{2}\sin\frac{A-B}{2},sinA−sinB=2cos2A+B​sin2A−B​, cos⁡A+cos⁡B=2cos⁡A+B2cos⁡A−B2,\cos A+\cos B=2\cos\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2},cosA+cosB=2cos2A+B​cos2A−B​, cos⁡A−cos⁡B=−2sin⁡A+B2sin⁡A−B2.\boxed{\cos A-\cos B =-2\sin\frac{A+B}{2}\sin\frac{A-B}{2}}.cosA−cosB=−2sin2A+B​sin2A−B​​.

Product forms:

2sin⁡Asin⁡B=cos⁡(A−B)−cos⁡(A+B),2\sin A\sin B=\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B),2sinAsinB=cos(A−B)−cos(A+B), 2cos⁡Acos⁡B=cos⁡(A−B)+cos⁡(A+B),2\cos A\cos B=\cos(A-B)+\cos(A+B),2cosAcosB=cos(A−B)+cos(A+B), 2sin⁡Acos⁡B=sin⁡(A+B)+sin⁡(A−B).2\sin A\cos B=\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B).2sinAcosB=sin(A+B)+sin(A−B).

Did you notice the clue? Angles in an arithmetic pattern, such as x,3x,5xx,3x,5xx,3x,5x, have a middle angle. Pair the outside terms:

sin⁡x+sin⁡5x=2sin⁡3xcos⁡2x.\sin x+\sin5x=2\sin3x\cos2x.sinx+sin5x=2sin3xcos2x.

The whole sum becomes sin⁡3x(1+2cos⁡2x)\sin3x(1+2\cos2x)sin3x(1+2cos2x). A product is useful for finding zeros because either factor can be zero.

For a numerical product, the opposite direction may be shorter. Pair 12∘,48∘12^\circ,48^\circ12∘,48∘ because their sum is 60∘60^\circ60∘ and difference is 36∘36^\circ36∘.

3u−4u3=1−2u2,3u-4u^3=1-2u^2,3u−4u3=1−2u2, (u−1)(4u2+2u−1)=0.(u-1)(4u^2+2u-1)=0.(u−1)(4u2+2u−1)=0.

Concept C11 — Telescoping and doubling products

Telescoping means adjacent terms cancel, leaving only the ends. From product-to-sum,

2sin⁡acos⁡((2j−1)a)=sin⁡(2ja)−sin⁡((2j−2)a).2\sin a\cos((2j-1)a) =\sin(2ja)-\sin((2j-2)a).2sinacos((2j−1)a)=sin(2ja)−sin((2j−2)a).

Adding from j=1j=1j=1 to nnn gives

∑j=1ncos⁡((2j−1)a)=sin⁡(2na)2sin⁡a,sin⁡a≠0.\boxed{\sum_{j=1}^n\cos((2j-1)a) =\frac{\sin(2na)}{2\sin a}},\qquad \sin a\ne0.j=1∑n​cos((2j−1)a)=2sinasin(2na)​​,sina=0.

More generally, for sin⁡(d/2)≠0\sin(d/2)\ne0sin(d/2)=0,

∑j=0n−1sin⁡(a+jd)=sin⁡(nd/2)sin⁡(d/2)sin⁡(a+(n−1)d2),\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\sin(a+jd) =\frac{\sin(nd/2)}{\sin(d/2)} \sin\left(a+\frac{(n-1)d}{2}\right),j=0∑n−1​sin(a+jd)=sin(d/2)sin(nd/2)​sin(a+2(n−1)d​), ∑j=0n−1cos⁡(a+jd)=sin⁡(nd/2)sin⁡(d/2)cos⁡(a+(n−1)d2).\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\cos(a+jd) =\frac{\sin(nd/2)}{\sin(d/2)} \cos\left(a+\frac{(n-1)d}{2}\right).j=0∑n−1​cos(a+jd)=sin(d/2)sin(nd/2)​cos(a+2(n−1)d​).

If d=2kπd=2k\pid=2kπ, the terms repeat identically; add nnn copies instead of dividing by zero.

Doubling-angle product: repeated use of sin⁡2a=2sin⁡acos⁡a\sin2a=2\sin a\cos asin2a=2sinacosa gives

cos⁡acos⁡2a⋯cos⁡(2m−1a)=sin⁡(2ma)2msin⁡a,sin⁡a≠0.\boxed{\cos a\cos2a\cdots\cos(2^{m-1}a) =\frac{\sin(2^ma)}{2^m\sin a}},\qquad\sin a\ne0.cosacos2a⋯cos(2m−1a)=2msinasin(2ma)​​,sina=0.

The clue is a,2a,4a,8aa,2a,4a,8aa,2a,4a,8a, not equally spaced angles. If sin⁡a=0\sin a=0sina=0, evaluate the original cosine factors directly.

Concept C12 — Equations: all angle families,then the interval

An identity is true for every input where defined. An equation asks which inputs work.

For real α\alphaα and integer nnn,

sin⁡x=sin⁡α  ⟺  x=nπ+(−1)nα,\boxed{\sin x=\sin\alpha \iff x=n\pi+(-1)^n\alpha},sinx=sinα⟺x=nπ+(−1)nα​,

or equivalently x=α+2nπx=\alpha+2n\pix=α+2nπ or x=π−α+2nπx=\pi-\alpha+2n\pix=π−α+2nπ.

cos⁡x=cos⁡α  ⟺  x=2nπ±α,\boxed{\cos x=\cos\alpha \iff x=2n\pi\pm\alpha},cosx=cosα⟺x=2nπ±α​, tan⁡x=tan⁡α  ⟺  x=nπ+α,\boxed{\tan x=\tan\alpha \iff x=n\pi+\alpha},tanx=tanα⟺x=nπ+α​,

with both tangent expressions defined. In particular,

sin⁡x=0⇒x=nπ,cos⁡x=0⇒x=π/2+nπ.\sin x=0\Rightarrow x=n\pi,\quad \cos x=0\Rightarrow x=\pi/2+n\pi.sinx=0⇒x=nπ,cosx=0⇒x=π/2+nπ.

If sin⁡x=c\sin x=csinx=c or cos⁡x=c\cos x=ccosx=c with ∣c∣>1|c|>1∣c∣>1, there is no real solution.

Four steps: keep the original domain; factor or reduce the equation; list all valid angle families; retain distinct angles inside the required interval.

For [0,2π][0,2\pi][0,2π], both endpoints are included and are different real numbers. A root that appears in two factor families is counted only once.

Do not divide by a factor that might be zero. In

cos⁡x(2sin⁡x−1)=0,\cos x(2\sin x-1)=0,cosx(2sinx−1)=0,

dividing by cos⁡x\cos xcosx loses the cos⁡x=0\cos x=0cosx=0 solutions.

Clearing a denominator is allowed only after noting its nonzero condition. Squaring can add roots, so check the original equation.

Concept C13 — Inequalities,modulus and parameter restrictions

For a polynomial in cos⁡x\cos xcosx, first solve for c=cos⁡xc=\cos xc=cosx within [−1,1][-1,1][−1,1]. Then read the cosine graph.

Here (2c−1)(c+1)≤0(2c-1)(c+1)\le0(2c−1)(c+1)≤0 gives −1≤c≤1/2-1\le c\le1/2−1≤c≤1/2. The graph gives x∈[π/3,5π/3]x\in[\pi/3,5\pi/3]x∈[π/3,5π/3].

Modulus is ordinary distance from zero:

∣u∣={u,u≥0,−u,u<0.|u|=\begin{cases}u,&u\ge0,\\-u,&u<0.\end{cases}∣u∣={u,−u,​u≥0,u<0.​

Its graph reflects any negative part above the axis. Thus ∣cos⁡x∣≥0|\cos x|\ge0∣cosx∣≥0. An equation ∣cos⁡x∣=sin⁡x|\cos x|=\sin x∣cosx∣=sinx first requires sin⁡x≥0\sin x\ge0sinx≥0. Squaring alone forgets this sign.

Parameter clue: if algebra gives sin⁡x=(k−4)/2\sin x=(k-4)/2sinx=(k−4)/2, existence of a real angle means

−1≤k−42≤1.-1\le\frac{k-4}{2}\le1.−1≤2k−4​≤1.

Solve this range condition before counting integer kkk. Endpoints are valid when sine reaches ±1\pm1±1.

Concept C14 — Maxima,minima and equality conditions

Cauchy–Schwarz — important for JEE Main:

(asin⁡x+bcos⁡x)2≤(a2+b2)(sin⁡2x+cos⁡2x)=a2+b2.\boxed{(a\sin x+b\cos x)^2 \le(a^2+b^2)(\sin^2x+\cos^2x)=a^2+b^2}.(asinx+bcosx)2≤(a2+b2)(sin2x+cos2x)=a2+b2​.

For the maximum +a2+b2+\sqrt{a^2+b^2}+a2+b2​, the coordinates (sin⁡x,cos⁡x)(\sin x,\cos x)(sinx,cosx) must point in the same direction as (a,b)(a,b)(a,b). The opposite direction gives the minimum. This explains the amplitude,including when equality occurs.

AM–GM — important for JEE Main: for positive u,vu,vu,v,

u+v≥2uv,u+v\ge2\sqrt{uv},u+v≥2uv​,

with equality exactly when u=vu=vu=v. For t>0t>0t>0 and A,B>0A,B>0A,B>0,

At+Bt≥2AB,t=BA at equality.\boxed{At+\frac Bt\ge2\sqrt{AB}}, \qquad t=\sqrt{\frac BA}\text{ at equality}.At+tB​≥2AB​​,t=AB​​ at equality.

A bound is not automatically the answer: the equality value must be allowed. Here t=tan⁡2θt=\tan^2\thetat=tan2θ can be any positive value,so t=2/3t=2/3t=2/3 is attainable.

Completing a square is often better for a quadratic. On a closed interval,check whether its vertex lies inside and compare the relevant endpoints for a maximum.

Concept C15 — Symmetric sums: calculate only the target

Put s=sin⁡x,c=cos⁡xs=\sin x,c=\cos xs=sinx,c=cosx. We know s2+c2=1s^2+c^2=1s2+c2=1. Therefore

(s+c)2=1+2sc,sc=(s+c)2−12.(s+c)^2=1+2sc,\qquad \boxed{sc=\frac{(s+c)^2-1}{2}}.(s+c)2=1+2sc,sc=2(s+c)2−1​​.

Also,

s3+c3=(s+c)(1−sc),s4+c4=1−2s2c2.\boxed{s^3+c^3=(s+c)(1-sc)},\qquad s^4+c^4=1-2s^2c^2.s3+c3=(s+c)(1−sc)​,s4+c4=1−2s2c2.

Did you notice the pattern? A given sum plus the circle identity already determines the product. That product then gives a cube or fourth-power sum. Finding the individual angle is unnecessary.

If tan⁡A,tan⁡B\tan A,\tan BtanA,tanB are roots of az2+bz+c=0az^2+bz+c=0az2+bz+c=0, Viète gives their sum −b/a-b/a−b/a and product c/ac/ac/a. Use

tan⁡(A+B)=tan⁡A+tan⁡B1−tan⁡Atan⁡B.\tan(A+B)=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}.tan(A+B)=1−tanAtanBtanA+tanB​.

Then use the actual angle interval to select the answer. Tangent equality alone determines an angle only up to multiples of π\piπ.

Concept C16 — Transcendental roots: graph first,prove the count

Sometimes an equation mixes a wave and a line,like sin⁡x=x/10\sin x=x/10sinx=x/10. There is no useful elementary formula for its nonzero roots.

The graph suggests the crossings. The proof needs more:

  1. ∣sin⁡x∣≤1|\sin x|\le1∣sinx∣≤1 gives ∣x∣≤10|x|\le10∣x∣≤10,so nothing outside this window can work.
  2. Odd symmetry pairs every positive root with one negative root.
  3. Signs and the shape on each positive hump establish the number of positive crossings.
  4. Count zero once.

For g(x)=sin⁡x−x/10g(x)=\sin x-x/10g(x)=sinx−x/10, g′′(x)=−sin⁡x<0g''(x)=-\sin x<0g′′(x)=−sinx<0 on a positive sine hump. The slope decreases there. This strict concavity,meaning the curve bends downward,prevents extra hidden crossings; Q2 develops the argument.

A sampled plot alone cannot prove the full root count. Conversely,searching for exact decimal roots is unnecessary when only the count is asked.

Concept C17 — Periods: repeating and the smallest repeat

A positive period TTT means f(x+T)=f(x)f(x+T)=f(x)f(x+T)=f(x) for every allowed input,with the domain preserved. The fundamental period is the smallest positive one,if it exists.

For nonzero real aaa,

Tsin⁡(ax+b)=Tcos⁡(ax+b)=2π∣a∣,Ttan⁡(ax+b)=π∣a∣.T_{\sin(ax+b)}=T_{\cos(ax+b)}=\frac{2\pi}{|a|}, \qquad T_{\tan(ax+b)}=\frac{\pi}{|a|}.Tsin(ax+b)​=Tcos(ax+b)​=∣a∣2π​,Ttan(ax+b)​=∣a∣π​.

The shift bbb moves the wave horizontally; it does not change its period. Squaring or taking modulus can shorten it:

Tsin⁡2x=Tcos⁡2x=T∣sin⁡x∣=T∣cos⁡x∣=π.T_{\sin^2x}=T_{\cos^2x}=T_{|\sin x|}=T_{|\cos x|}=\pi.Tsin2x​=Tcos2x​=T∣sinx∣​=T∣cosx∣​=π.

A common period of two summands is a period of their sum. It need not always be fundamental: sin⁡x−sin⁡x=0\sin x-\sin x=0sinx−sinx=0 is constant and has every positive period.

For sin⁡(x/3)+cos⁡(x/2)\sin(x/3)+\cos(x/2)sin(x/3)+cos(x/2),the two nonzero distinct frequencies do not cancel. A period must preserve both frequencies. One rigorous reason is that sine and cosine at different nonzero frequencies are linearly independent: their coefficients in an identity cannot cancel each other. This can be checked by differentiating twice to separate the two frequencies. Thus

T/3=2mπ,T/2=2nπ,T/3=2m\pi,\quad T/2=2n\pi,T/3=2mπ,T/2=2nπ,

so the smallest positive common value is T=12πT=12\piT=12π. For sums,check frequency cancellation before using an LCM shortcut.

Worked solutions to the 30 PDF questions

Read the question first. Notice the pattern, choose a route, then calculate. Alternative methods below are fully visible.

Question 1 — Pair the angles before multiplying

PDF page 130 | MCQ | Notes: C05,C09,C10

The value of sin⁡12∘sin⁡48∘sin⁡54∘\sin12^\circ\sin48^\circ\sin54^\circsin12∘sin48∘sin54∘ is

  • (a) 116\frac1{16}161​
  • (b) 38\frac{\sqrt3}{8}83​​
  • (c) 18\frac1881​
  • (d) 14\frac1441​

Did you notice two useful pairs? 12∘+48∘=60∘12^\circ+48^\circ=60^\circ12∘+48∘=60∘ and 48∘−12∘=36∘48^\circ-12^\circ=36^\circ48∘−12∘=36∘. Also sin⁡54∘=cos⁡36∘\sin54^\circ=\cos36^\circsin54∘=cos36∘. These connections are more useful than finding three separate decimal sine values.

Let c=cos⁡36∘c=\cos36^\circc=cos36∘. Product-to-sum gives

2sin⁡12∘sin⁡48∘=cos⁡36∘−cos⁡60∘=c−12.2\sin12^\circ\sin48^\circ =\cos36^\circ-\cos60^\circ=c-\frac12.2sin12∘sin48∘=cos36∘−cos60∘=c−21​.

Thus the required product is 12c(c−12)\frac12c(c-\frac12)21​c(c−21​). From the notes,

c=5+14,c−12=5−14.c=\frac{\sqrt5+1}{4},\qquad c-\frac12=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{4}.c=45​+1​,c−21​=45​−1​.

Therefore

12(5+1)(5−1)16=12416=18;(c).\boxed{\frac12\frac{(\sqrt5+1)(\sqrt5-1)}{16} =\frac12\frac4{16}=\frac18;\quad\text{(c)}}.21​16(5​+1)(5​−1)​=21​164​=81​;(c)​.

Check: all three original angles are acute,so the product is positive. The product-to-sum step contributes a factor 1/21/21/2; do not lose it.

Question 2 — Count crossings rather than search for exact roots

PDF page 130 | Numerical value | Notes: C03,C16

The number of real solutions of the equation sin⁡x=x10\sin x=\frac{x}{10}sinx=10x​ is ____.

This asks for a count,not exact root values. Visualize intersections of y=sin⁡xy=\sin xy=sinx and y=x/10y=x/10y=x/10. Since ∣sin⁡x∣≤1|\sin x|\le1∣sinx∣≤1, every root must satisfy ∣x∣≤10|x|\le10∣x∣≤10.

Put g(x)=sin⁡x−x/10g(x)=\sin x-x/10g(x)=sinx−x/10. It is odd: g(−x)=−g(x)g(-x)=-g(x)g(−x)=−g(x). Thus positive roots have negative partners,and zero is a root.

For x>0x>0x>0,the line is positive,so only positive sine humps can contain roots:

  1. On (0,π)(0,\pi)(0,π): g(0)=0g(0)=0g(0)=0, g′(0)=9/10>0g'(0)=9/10>0g′(0)=9/10>0, and g(π)=−π/10<0g(\pi)=-\pi/10<0g(π)=−π/10<0. Also g′′=−sin⁡x<0g''=-\sin x<0g′′=−sinx<0,so the slope decreases strictly. The curve first rises,then falls,and crosses zero exactly once after its maximum.
  2. On (π,2π)(\pi,2\pi)(π,2π): sine is nonpositive while the line is positive,so there is no root.
  3. On (2π,3π)(2\pi,3\pi)(2π,3π): both endpoints have g<0g<0g<0,but
g(5π/2)=1−π4>0.g(5\pi/2)=1-\frac\pi4>0.g(5π/2)=1−4π​>0.

On this hump the slope again decreases strictly,from 9/109/109/10 to −11/10-11/10−11/10. There is one maximum,one crossing before it and one after it: exactly two roots.

  1. On (3π,10](3\pi,10](3π,10]: sine is negative because 3π<10<4π3\pi<10<4\pi3π<10<4π,so there is no root.

There are 1+2=31+2=31+2=3 positive roots. Hence

3+3+1=7.\boxed{3+3+1=7}.3+3+1=7​.

Why the picture alone is insufficient: a coarse plot can hide crossings. The domain bound,signs and decreasing slope establish that none are missed. Numerically finding all six nonzero roots would be longer and would not by itself prove completeness.

Question 3 — Change a tangent into sine divided by cosine

PDF page 130 | MCQ | Notes: C02,C09

The value of tan⁡20∘+4sin⁡20∘\tan20^\circ+4\sin20^\circtan20∘+4sin20∘ is

  • (a) 3\sqrt33​
  • (b) 32\frac{\sqrt3}{2}23​​
  • (c) 232\sqrt323​
  • (d) 111

Tangent is a quotient. Start with a common denominator:

tan⁡20∘+4sin⁡20∘=sin⁡20∘+4sin⁡20∘cos⁡20∘cos⁡20∘.\tan20^\circ+4\sin20^\circ =\frac{\sin20^\circ+4\sin20^\circ\cos20^\circ}{\cos20^\circ}.tan20∘+4sin20∘=cos20∘sin20∘+4sin20∘cos20∘​.

The product suggests a double angle:

4sin⁡20∘cos⁡20∘=2sin⁡40∘.4\sin20^\circ\cos20^\circ=2\sin40^\circ.4sin20∘cos20∘=2sin40∘.

Now group the numerator as (sin⁡20∘+sin⁡40∘)+sin⁡40∘(\sin20^\circ+\sin40^\circ)+\sin40^\circ(sin20∘+sin40∘)+sin40∘:

sin⁡20∘+sin⁡40∘=2sin⁡30∘cos⁡10∘=cos⁡10∘=sin⁡80∘.\sin20^\circ+\sin40^\circ =2\sin30^\circ\cos10^\circ =\cos10^\circ=\sin80^\circ.sin20∘+sin40∘=2sin30∘cos10∘=cos10∘=sin80∘.

One more sum-to-product step gives

sin⁡80∘+sin⁡40∘=2sin⁡60∘cos⁡20∘=3cos⁡20∘.\sin80^\circ+\sin40^\circ =2\sin60^\circ\cos20^\circ =\sqrt3\cos20^\circ.sin80∘+sin40∘=2sin60∘cos20∘=3​cos20∘.

Since cos⁡20∘≠0\cos20^\circ\ne0cos20∘=0,

3cos⁡20∘cos⁡20∘=3;(a).\boxed{\frac{\sqrt3\cos20^\circ}{\cos20^\circ} =\sqrt3;\quad\text{(a)}}.cos20∘3​cos20∘​=3​;(a)​.

Pattern to keep: converting tangent to a quotient reveals a product; converting that product to a double angle reveals a pair of sine sums. This route avoids complicated exact individual values at 20∘20^\circ20∘.

Question 4 — A quadratic in sine gives several angle positions

PDF page 130 | MCQ | Notes: C06,C12

The sum of all solutions of 2cos⁡2x+3sin⁡x=32\cos^2x+3\sin x=32cos2x+3sinx=3 in [0,2π][0,2\pi][0,2π] is

  • (a) π\piπ
  • (b) 2π2\pi2π
  • (c) 5π2\frac{5\pi}{2}25π​
  • (d) 3π2\frac{3\pi}{2}23π​

There are two functions,but the circle identity can leave only one. Put s=sin⁡xs=\sin xs=sinx and use cos⁡2x=1−s2\cos^2x=1-s^2cos2x=1−s2:

2(1−s2)+3s=3⟹2s2−3s+1=(2s−1)(s−1)=0.2(1-s^2)+3s=3 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 2s^2-3s+1=(2s-1)(s-1)=0.2(1−s2)+3s=3⟹2s2−3s+1=(2s−1)(s−1)=0.

Thus sin⁡x=1/2\sin x=1/2sinx=1/2 or sin⁡x=1\sin x=1sinx=1.

In [0,2π][0,2\pi][0,2π],

sin⁡x=12⇒x=π6,5π6,sin⁡x=1⇒x=π2.\sin x=\frac12\Rightarrow x=\frac\pi6,\frac{5\pi}6, \qquad \sin x=1\Rightarrow x=\frac\pi2.sinx=21​⇒x=6π​,65π​,sinx=1⇒x=2π​.

Neither endpoint is a solution. Add the three distinct angles:

π6+π2+5π6=3π2;(d).\boxed{\frac\pi6+\frac\pi2+\frac{5\pi}6 =\frac{3\pi}{2};\quad\text{(d)}}.6π​+2π​+65π​=23π​;(d)​.

Check: substituting either sine value into the reduced equation works. One algebraic sine root can give two angles; count angles,not just polynomial roots.

Question 5 — A cube sum is already hidden in the given sum

PDF page 130 | Numerical value | Notes: C06,C15

If sin⁡θ+cos⁡θ=12\sin\theta+\cos\theta=\frac12sinθ+cosθ=21​, then 16(sin⁡3θ+cos⁡3θ)16(\sin^3\theta+\cos^3\theta)16(sin3θ+cos3θ) equals ____.

The target is a cube sum. It suggests

s3+c3=(s+c)3−3sc(s+c),s=sin⁡θ, c=cos⁡θ.s^3+c^3=(s+c)^3-3sc(s+c), \qquad s=\sin\theta,\ c=\cos\theta.s3+c3=(s+c)3−3sc(s+c),s=sinθ, c=cosθ.

We already know s+c=1/2s+c=1/2s+c=1/2 and s2+c2=1s^2+c^2=1s2+c2=1. Square the given sum to find the missing product:

14=(s+c)2=1+2sc⟹sc=−38.\frac14=(s+c)^2=1+2sc \quad\Longrightarrow\quad sc=-\frac38.41​=(s+c)2=1+2sc⟹sc=−83​.

Now

s3+c3=(s+c)(s2−sc+c2)=12(1+38)=1116.s^3+c^3=(s+c)(s^2-sc+c^2) =\frac12\left(1+\frac38\right)=\frac{11}{16}.s3+c3=(s+c)(s2−sc+c2)=21​(1+83​)=1611​. 16(s3+c3)=11.\boxed{16(s^3+c^3)=11}.16(s3+c3)=11​.

Another possible approach: use (1/2)3−3(−3/8)(1/2)=1/8+9/16=11/16(1/2)^3-3(-3/8)(1/2)=1/8+9/16=11/16(1/2)3−3(−3/8)(1/2)=1/8+9/16=11/16 directly.

Solving for θ\thetaθ creates unnecessary branches. The symmetric target needs only the sum and product.

Question 6 — The variable sin squared lives only between zero and one

PDF page 130 | MCQ | Notes: C06,C14

Consider the function f(x)=sin⁡2x+cos⁡4xf(x)=\sin^2x+\cos^4xf(x)=sin2x+cos4x.

Statement I: The minimum value of f(x)f(x)f(x) is 34\frac3443​.

Statement II: The maximum value of f(x)f(x)f(x) is 111.

Choose the correct option.

  • (a) Statement I is true and Statement II is false
  • (b) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
  • (c) Statement I is false and Statement II is true
  • (d) Both Statement I and Statement II are false

(d) 0<2<3<π0<2<3<\pi0<2<3<π,where cosine decreases. Thus cos⁡3<cos⁡2\cos3<\cos2cos3<cos2. True.

(a), (b), (d) only; (d).\boxed{\text{(a), (b), (d) only; (d)}}.(a), (b), (d) only; (d)​.

Another check: numerical values can confirm these comparisons,but monotonic intervals explain them and avoid mixing degrees with radians.

Question 21 — Modulus forces a sign condition before squaring

cos⁡2x=sin⁡2x⟹sin⁡2x=12.\cos^2x=\sin^2x \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \sin^2x=\frac12.cos2x=sin2x⟹sin2x=21​.

Within [0,4π][0,4\pi][0,4π],

x=π4,3π4,9π4,11π4.x=\frac\pi4,\frac{3\pi}4,\frac{9\pi}4,\frac{11\pi}4.x=4π​,43π​,49π​,411π​. 4.\boxed{4}.4​.

cos⁡x=0⇒x=π2,3π2,\cos x=0\Rightarrow x=\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2,cosx=0⇒x=2π​,23π​, sin⁡x=12⇒x=π6,5π6.\sin x=\frac12\Rightarrow x=\frac\pi6,\frac{5\pi}6.sinx=21​⇒x=6π​,65π​.

Question 30 — The quadratic already gives the tangent sum and product

If tan⁡A\tan AtanA and tan⁡B\tan BtanB are the roots of 6x2−5x+1=06x^2-5x+1=06x2−5x+1=0 with A,BA,BA,B acute, then A+BA+BA+B (in degrees) is ____.

tan⁡(A+B)=5/61−1/6=1.\tan(A+B)=\frac{5/6}{1-1/6}=1.tan(A+B)=1−1/65/6​=1.

A+B=45∘.\boxed{A+B=45^\circ}.A+B=45∘​.
